html:
Mundurukânia is the homeland of the Munduruku, who call themselves Wuy jugu, a Tupian people of the Tapajós River basin in the Brazilian Amazon, in Pará and Amazonas.

The Munduruku were feared warriors. In the 1700s they raided far across the Amazon and kept the heads of enemies as trophies. They made peace with Portuguese Brazil in the 1790s and then fought for the Portuguese against other peoples. During the rubber boom many were drawn into tapping rubber. Their villages, with a men's house at the centre, became well known to anthropologists. Today the Munduruku number over ten thousand and have led protests against dams and illegal gold mining on the Tapajós. Their neighbours to the north include the Sateré-Mawé.
